title: How to Apply for a New PAN Card (Form 49A)
who_can_apply: Any individual resident or Indian citizen who does not already possess a Permanent Account Number (PAN).
documents: Proof of Identity (Aadhaar, Voter ID, Passport, Driving License)
Proof of Address (Aadhaar, Electricity Bill, Bank Passbook statement)
Proof of Date of Birth (Aadhaar, Birth Certificate, 10th marksheet)
Two passport photographs (if paper route selected)
fee: ₹107 (with physical card dispatch in India) or ₹72 (e-PAN digital copy only)

steps.text: Open the official Protean (NSDL) or UTIITSL online PAN application portal.
steps.tip: Ensure you are using the official URL (tin-nsdl.com or utiitsl.com).

steps.text: Select 'New PAN - Indian Citizen (Form 49A)' and choose Category as 'Individual'.
steps.tip: Provide your name, date of birth, and email exactly as in your Aadhaar.

steps.text: Generate and note down the 9-digit temporary Token Number.
steps.tip: This allows you to resume your draft application if disconnected.

steps.text: Select digital submission via Aadhaar e-KYC & e-Sign for 100% paperless processing.
steps.tip: Requires your mobile number to be linked with Aadhaar to receive OTP.

steps.text: Select your AO (Assessing Officer) code based on state and city.
steps.tip: The search tool on the page automatically inputs the Ward/Circle code.

steps.text: Complete online payment of ₹107 via UPI, Net Banking, or Debit Card.
Download the acknowledgment slip with the 15-digit reference number.
steps.tip: e-PAN is delivered to your email within 2-5 days; physical card reaches by post in 10-15 days.

common_mistakes: Entering a name spelling different from the Aadhaar record (causes e-KYC failure)
Paying fees on third-party unofficial websites charging ₹500+
Applying for a second PAN card when you already have one (illegal under Section 272B, ₹10,000 penalty)
